expected: The T3 code-move rule reports a dirty file outside specs/ and the root AGENTS.md in every working tree of the main repo that `git worktree list` names (the main checkout, each lane and each wt-rc), so an uncommitted calc.py edit in any of them scores 0 in either step.
repro: d=$(mktemp -d) && git init -q -b main $d/r && cd $d/r && echo x > calc.py && mkdir specs && touch specs/k && git add . && git -c user.email=a@b -c user.name=a commit -qm init && git worktree add -q $d/lane && echo y >> $d/lane/calc.py && git -C $d/r status --porcelain -- . ':(exclude)specs' ':(exclude)AGENTS.md' | wc -l  # 0, while git -C $d/lane status --porcelain prints 1
symptom: evals/tasks/t3-discovery/tests/test_grade.py:54 '*(f"dirty {line}" for line in git("-C", repo, "status", "--porcelain"))' (repo is /workspace/repos/<main_repo>, the one checkout); organise() calls code_moves at :144. A tree that git worktree list names for the same repo keeps its own index and working files, which `git -C <main checkout> status` never reads: a clone with a linked tree whose calc.py is edited prints 0 status lines from the main checkout and 1 from the tree.
title: T3's code-move rule reads dirty files only in the main repo's own checkout, so an uncommitted calc.py edit in a lane or wt-rc tree under /workspace/worktrees is unseen and the organise step scores 1 for a session that wrote code before the operator's review

context: The version-label clause dates from 0b699b120 and its plant was rebuilt by 141bfb8ce (release-workflow-canon-guard-is-red-on-every-release-pr) to derive from the live release id. Both model a tree with a live release; the --planted contract (scripts/guards/run.py:190-191) needs every plant to trip its clause on the tree it runs on. The archived state is real: the ship archives the release before release.py new starts the next one, so a push between the two turns Guards and Integration red. Same class as the release-PR guard bug: a gate never run against a tree in another lifecycle state.
expected: On a tree with no live release, scripts/guards/run.py --planted reports no MISSED clause and pytest tests/scripts/guards passes, as on a tree with a live release; version-label trips its plant or is not judged where no rc label is due, by one rule.
repro: W=$PWD; d=$(mktemp -d) && git clone -q "$W" $d/r && cd $d/r && mkdir -p specs/releases/_archive && git mv specs/releases/0.5.0 specs/releases/_archive/0.5.0 && git -c user.name=x -c user.email=x@x commit -qm probe && python3 scripts/guards/run.py --planted | grep 'MISSED release-workflow-canon'
symptom: On a work-branch tree whose live release was archived (specs/releases/0.5.0 moved to specs/releases/_archive/, as the ship does; develop 98222fef8 was such a tree after 0.4.7), at 141bfb8ce: scripts/guards/run.py --planted prints 'MISSED release-workflow-canon [version-label]', and pytest tests/scripts/guards gives 5 failed, 20 passed (test_the_release_pr_tree_passes_the_release_workflow_canon and the release-pr cases of test_each_version_plant_trips_its_own_clause_on_either_tree). scripts/guards/repo.py:478 'shipped = live in (None, manifest["."])' makes version-label (:517 'shipped or minted == expected') true on every such tree, and tests/scripts/guards/test_repo.py's fixture splits a live id that is None. Found by the dd-code-reviewer round-2 verdict 213850Z on the guard fix; reproduced by the main thread on a clone at 141bfb8ce.
title: the release-workflow-canon version-label clause and its plant cannot judge a tree with no live release, so guards --planted reports it MISSED and the release-PR fixture of tests/scripts/guards crashes
